links.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of LLM-generated CRC patient education materials versus recommended levels
links.effect: Readability consistently exceeded recommended levels for patient materials, with FKGL scores typically corresponding to US grades 7–10.
links.quote: Readability consistently exceeded recommended levels for patient materials, with FKGL scores typically corresponding to US grades 7–10.

links.outcome: Reading level of LLM patient education text relative to appropriate patient reading level
links.effect: Outputs consistently failed to meet recommended readability standards; FKGL typically US grades 7–10; Gemini-2.5Pro responses longer and more complex.
links.quote: Outputs consistently fail to meet recommended readability standards, potentially hindering comprehension for many patients.

links.outcome: Presence of citations or information sources in LLM outputs
links.effect: None of the four models provided citations or information sources.
links.quote: Critically, none of the four models provided citations or information sources.

links.outcome: Whether LLM answers displayed supporting sources
links.effect: None of the four models provided citations or information sources, compromising transparency and trustworthiness.
links.quote: While demonstrating ‘fair’ quality, the universal lack of source citations severely compromises transparency and trustworthiness.

screen.reason: Evaluates the baseline readability, quality (DISCERN), and transparency of four commercial LLMs generating colorectal cancer patient education materials without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
